content.title: When are taxes due in 2026?
content.text: Whether you're filing as an individual, business owner, or freelancer, knowing your deadlines for 2026 can make a big difference in managing stress and staying compliant. In this guide, we’ll walk you through everything you need to know about when taxes are due in 2026, key IRS dates, and tips for preparing early so you’re not scrambling at the last minute. Missing deadlines means hefty IRS penalty and interest charges, or extended delays receiving that nice refund you have been relying on. Key tax deadlines for 2026 Federal Tax Day: April 15, 2026 (Wednesday)Mark your calendar: April 15, 2026 is the deadline to file your federal income taxes for the 2025 tax year. Since it falls on a Wednesday and isn’t a federal holiday, no extensions are expected unless announced by the IRS. Whether you're filing a 1040, 1040A, 1040EZ, or any other version of the 1040, this is the big day. Additional Important Tax Dates Jan 15, 2026: Q4 2025 Estimated Tax Payment Due (self-employed, freelancers, investors) Jan 31, 2026: Deadline for employers to send out W-2s and 1099s March 17, 2026 (because the 15th falls on a weekend): Deadline for businesses to file S-Corp and Partnership returns April 15, 2026: Tax filing deadline for 2025 + first estimated payment for 2026 Extended deadline for S-Corp and Partnership businesses to file 2025 taxes (if extension is filed by March 17) Oct 15, 2026: Extended deadline to file 2025 taxes (if extension is filed by April 15) Extension Deadline TimingIf April 15 is coming too fast, don’t panic. You can file Form 4868 for an automatic 6-month extension to file your return. This gives you until October 15, 2026 to submit your completed forms. But here’s the catch: the extension only applies to filing. If you owe taxes, you still need to pay by April 15th to avoid late payment penalties and interest. Tips for a smoother tax season 1. Organize Your Documents EarlyStart a tax folder (digital or physical) and collect: W-2s, 1099s Bank and brokerage statements Charitable donation receipts Business income and expenses (if applicable) 2. Adjust Your WithholdingDid you owe a lot or get a big refund this year? Consider adjusting your W-4 form to better match your actual tax liability for 2026. 3. Contribute to Tax-Advantaged AccountsMax out your IRA or HSA before the deadline to potentially reduce your taxable income. The deadline for these contributions is typically the same as Tax Day. Let Liberty Tax Help Filing taxes doesn’t have to feel like a fire drill. With a few early steps and a clear understanding of the deadlines, you’ll be in great shape. Remember: April 15, 2026 is the big day. FIND A LOCAL OFFICEStay organized, connect with your local Liberty Tax expert, and keep an eye on any IRS updates throughout the year.
